When words sound the same but have a different meaning, they are called homophones.
A homophone is a word that has the same sound as another word but has a different meaning and may have a different spelling.

For example: right and write
right (noun) and right (adjective)

Stressing Two Syllables Back From the Suffix: -ize
When you say words that end with the suffix -ize, you stress the third syllable from the end of the word, or two syllables before the -ize suffix.
Read these words out loud. Concentrate on the pronunciation. Put the stress two syllables before the -ize suffix.

images.text: Amy: Welcome to our mindfulness session. Instead of giving others a piece of your mind because of something they have done to negatively affect you, we are going to gain peace of mind through mindfulness meditation. We are going to stop spending our days in a daze and learn to be present. Everyone's presence is like many presents or gifts to our fellow friends. We don't need to compromise anything with mindfulness.

How many of you wake up on a sunny morning to  the sun's rays and realize the beauty and calm of that moment? Raise your hands when you feel a sense of joy. Yes,  I see a few of you. The effects of mindfulness  affect your physiology  so that you can have more beautiful moments like these.

Our session today will be one hour of meditation. To make this practice part of your daily routine you don't have to memorize anything. You will follow a meditation in which you visualize yourself and your body relaxing .You will allow the stress to melt away and focus your attention on your breath at first. Then you will try to clear your mind of all thought.  With daily practice, mindfulness meditation allows us to use more of our brain capacity and makes us more compassionate and forgiving individuals.To initialize this process we will all find a cushion and a spot on the floor. Sit in a cross-legged position and gently close your eyes.
